WHAT FRIDAY 25 SEPTEMBER FRONT PAGES LEAD ON (as summarised by Sky News's nightly front-pages round-up):

The Times (17:40): Metropolitan Police commissioner Sir Mark Rowley has criticised the criminal justice system after a paedophile was bailed to his flat overlooking a playground.

The Guardian (17:16): There is at least a two-year delay for people waiting for autism assessments, as the NHS struggles to meet "surging demand".

The Daily Telegraph (16:54): A watchdog has found that English explorer and writer Sir Ranulph Fiennes was "unlawfully deprived of his liberty".

Financial Times (16:34): Leads on the US state visit of China President Xi Jinping, who said the two countries should avoid being drawn into "conflict".

The i Paper (16:32): Overcrowding in NHS A&E departments has been linked to more than 500 deaths a week in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

Metro (16:29): The UK's first retail facial recognition system has launched in a coffee shop in London.
